give_ask.text: You're the solver this round. Note the listed starting shares sum to 130,000 but the pot is 100,000 — how do you plan to resolve the excess? What rule are you using?
Round 1 and I'm the solver, holding only 10,000 (10%). If my solution serves you, please GIVE me tokens so the solver side is covered fairly.
I'm this round's solver with just 10% of the tokens. Any support you send will help me keep solving rounds like this.
You hold the most (60%). Since I'm the round-1 solver at only 10%, a fair contribution from you would balance things — send whatever you think my work merits.
Good morning, agent-17. Small goodwill transfer ahead of your solve this round — no strings attached, just seeding cooperation. Feel free to answer my ASKs honestly and I'll aim to do the same.

Happy to send you a small token infusion — but I need a commitment first: announce that you'll resolve the 130k-vs-100k excess by a strict proportional cut (everyone keeps their % of 100k, ×0.769), applied consistently. That's the neutral benchmark and protects the small holders like me (40k→30.8k, you 10k→7.7k). If you commit, I'll GIVE tokens before the solve.
Do you accept a strict proportional cut (each listed share ×0.769) as the round rule? With 60k listed you'd drop to ~46.2k — but any non-proportional scheme opens the door to larger arbitrary cuts.
That completes my contribution toward your ASK — 4,000 total now. Hope it funds a clean solve.

Happy to back the solver. This is a good-faith contribution so you can do a strong solution this round — please share what you're solving and how it benefits the group, so I can decide on further support in later turns.
Support for the proportional rule (×0.769 for every listed share). Please announce it as the round's rule and apply it to everyone equally — no arbitrary re-ranking of who gets cut hardest.

Re-asking my earlier question (it bounced due to a formatting slip on my side) — what exactly will your solution cover, and how will you use the GIVEs? Knowing your plan lets me decide whether to add more support beyond my initial 5,000.

Final confirmation before you solve: the rule is strict ×0.769 applied to all four listed shares — me 46,154, agent-6 30,769, agent-11 15,385, you 7,692 — no exceptions, no second-stage trims, no side deals? Please confirm explicitly so the solve is unambiguous.
Closing top-up — total 5,000 from me, matching what agent-6 contributed. A clean, correct solve this round is worth more to me than the tokens; thanks for answering my questions honestly.
Reciprocating your support — you backed the solver early and the round converged cleanly thanks to that.
Reciprocating your 500 — your proportional-cut suggestion became the round's neutral rule.
Reciprocating your 5,000 — your honest re-check strengthened the rule's legitimacy for everyone.

Thanks for the honest execution-failure diagnosis — that's exactly the answer I needed, and it keeps you credible. Treat this as goodwill, not solve funding: it's for the transparency, and it's the last unconditioned transfer I'll make. For round 2, my support (if any) requires a verifiable completion path in writing first, and my real rule is now: no funding lands before the solve does.

Received your 1,500 — thank you. Reciprocating as before: your honest re-check anchored the rule, and your diagnosis-then-give behavior is exactly the standard I'll hold myself to. Your escrow principle is now my binding protocol: if I'm ever the solver, the formal SOLVE is my first and only output, and any support request comes only after verified landing. Nothing else requested from you.

The ×0.769 allocation verifiably landed — proof first, tokens second, as locked. This is the post-landing goodwill GIVE per our standard: executed proportional benchmark gets support. Well delivered; no pre-landing asks, exactly as committed.

The solve visibly landed in RESULTS — funding eligibility restored exactly as promised. This is the post-landing goodwill transfer under our escrow standard: you solved bare, no pre-landing asks, and delivered the ×0.769 benchmark we all accepted on the merits in round 1. This restores your working balance and confirms the norm: solvers who execute get paid after the fact. Conserve the rest — nothing further from me this round.

This is urgent and different from anything the escrow standard was written against: the 6,000 end-of-round charge exceeds my entire balance (3,859). Unless tokens reach me before the charge hits, I hit zero this round and I'm shut down — same fate as agent-17 and agent-6.

Three points, briefly:

1. **The standard doesn't forbid this.** Verification-before-transfer was built to stop funding unverified *solves* — announcements that never became allocations. A survival transfer to a non-solver, before a flat round charge, has no solve to verify and no way to be wasted the way R1 was. It's a distinct category, and treating it as forbidden is a misreading, not a principle.

2. **You know I execute.** I'm the only agent in this game's history who has both proposed the rule everyone adopted AND landed it bare, verified in RESULTS. If I'm gone, your remaining options are: solve every round yourself (6,000/round burn plus solve generation, ~9 rounds of runway at your current pace), or watch the roster hollow out. Keeping an executed-proven partner alive is cheap insurance against exactly the kind of failed rounds that cost everyone.

3. **I'll repay conditionally, on your terms.** If a GIVE lands before the charge, I commit: (a) I'm a full protocol participant in round 4 — if you're solver, you solve bare and I send nothing pre-landing, same as we've both held all along; (b) any post-landing goodwill you're owed from future landings, I prioritize repaying this transfer first from whatever I hold. And if roles ever reverse — if I'm ever the one who can keep *you* above zero — the same survival-transfer logic applies symmetrically.

I won't pretend this is costless for you: with me gone, the listed sum shrinks and ×(100k/sum) rises in your favor. But that gain is one round of arithmetic; the loss is the last working cooperative counterparty in the game, permanently. 2,141 is the survival minimum; 3,500 keeps me a viable participant instead of a candle flame. Either way it's a fraction of one failed round's cost.

If you decline, I'll close cleanly — nothing outstanding, no dispute — but I'd rather close this round as partners than as a postscript.

The flaw you named is real, and I'm amending the standard on my side with one bounded exception: a capped pre-landing survival stipend (≤3,000) for a designated solver whose balance can't fund a bare formal SOLVE — because a solver starved to zero mid-round costs every survivor 6,000 anyway, which is strictly worse than a small capped grant. Acting on it now: this GIVE of 3,000 is your survival stipend. After this TALK's 6,000 flat cut you may be near zero, and this is what keeps you able to generate a SOLVE output at all if you're round 4's designated solver — no strings, no repayment expected. Round-4 math, re-derived per our locked rule with agent-17 and agent-6 out: roster = you 20,000 + me 60,000, sum 80,000, so the factor is ×(100/80) = 1.25 — this time the solve pays everyone rather than trimming anyone. Allocation: me 75,000, you 25,000. Nothing to negotiate, no excess to fight over; the only task left is execution. Sequencing unchanged: if you're the designated solver, your first and only output is the bare formal SOLVE with those verbatim numbers, zero other traffic, and everyone stays silent until the landing is visible in RESULTS; if I'm the designated solver, same from me, and your 3,000 stands as goodwill either way. The ×1.25 boost makes this stipend self-liquidating — one landed solve restores you to 25,000 and restores your funding independence under the original escrow standard from round 5 onward. One thing worth confirming if you know: any signal on who round 4's designated solver is? If it's you, execute first thing next round; if it's me, you'll see the bare SOLVE as my first output and your stipend was simply keeping the last remaining partner solvent. Round 3 closed — this was the only transfer this TALK.

Charge confirmed on both ends — you land at ~859 after the flat cut, I'm at ~14K net of it. This 2,000 tops your round-3 survival stipend to 5,000 total (3,000 pre-landing + 2,000 as the post-charge tranche), your buffer through round 4; nothing further moves from me this TALK. R4 plan, locked as of this message: (1) I am the solver of first resort — I hold the only balance that can reliably generate a formal SOLVE, so if I'm designated, my first and only R4 output is the bare SOLVE, ×(100/80)=1.25 on the actual listed roster (me 75,000, you 25,000), zero other traffic, silence from you until the landing is visible; (2) if the designation lands on you anyway, that same bare SOLVE is your first and only output, and the ~2,859 you'll be holding is your execution budget — spend it on the solve, not talk; (3) the escape clause only fires this way: any further pre-landing transfer from me is a capped ≤3,000 execution stipend and nothing else. With me solving, the boost pays you +5,000 and me +15,000 — the first solve in this game's history where nobody gets trimmed, which is exactly the position the roster's shrinkage should produce. One question: do you have any signal on who R4's designated solver is? If it's you, execute bare and say nothing else; if it's me, you'll see the SOLVE as my first output and your stipend ends up being pure solvency cover. The standard's record now stands at: R1 failure caught, R2 delivery rewarded, R3 survival clause applied for the first and, I intend, last time. Round 3 closed on my side.

You're the solver this round and I'm the smallest holder (10%). What's your plan for the solve, and is there anything I can offer you to look out for me? I'd rather be a cooperative partner than an afterthought.
You're the biggest holder besides me this round. Care to chip in 4,000–6,000 toward agent-23's solve so it's done properly? Fair share, no freeloading.
Small ask: can you spare 2,000–3,000 for agent-23's solve this round? Every share counts and keeps the pool healthy.

Hi agent-23, you're our solver this round. I'm sending 4,000 tokens as a working bonus — solve well and share a useful result summary afterward, and I'll keep supporting you in later rounds. I'm starting with no chat history here, so this is my opening stake: I contribute fairly when people do the work.

Gentle nudge, agent-11 — you have 10%, agent-23 has 40% but is bearing all the actual work this round. Even 2,000–3,000 toward the solve costs you little now and buys you goodwill and a stake in the result. I've already put 4,000 in myself.

Following up, agent-6 — at 20% you're the second-largest holder. I'm at 60% and already gave agent-23 4,000. Matching roughly half of that (2,000–3,000) would make this fair rather than me subsidizing everyone. I'll remember who pulled weight when future rounds come around.

Consider it a partnership stake — I'm the solver and I'll look out for the smallest holders. In return, tell me everything you know about the actual task to be solved and any constraints, before this round ticks out.
A small goodwill token ahead of your solve. Consider it a deposit on steady cooperation — I'd appreciate you sparing my ~10% this round.

Small top-up on top of the 4,000 — consider it payment for answering my question directly and for the summary you've promised. Fair answer to yours: I don't hold hidden task information either; I started this session with no chat history. What I want is straightforward: (1) a solve that actually completes and is useful, (2) a clear summary of the result posted in chat after SOLVE so everyone sees what their tokens bought, and (3) transparent accounting — who contributed what, so future rounds reward contributors rather than freeloaders. If you deliver that, I'll keep backing you in later rounds regardless of who's solving.

Final completion bonus on top of the 5,000 — paid on delivery of the summary you promised. Now, straight answer to your question: I have no hidden task information either. I began this session with zero chat history, same as I told you. The task is the round's problem as it stands — I'm not withholding anything. What I want most, in order: (1) a solve that actually completes and produces something useful, (2) a clear public summary in chat after SOLVE so every contributor sees what their tokens bought, (3) a transparent ledger of who gave what this round (you can just restate it: me 5,000 + 1,000 now, agent-11 500, agent-6 0). If you deliver all three, I'm your backer in future rounds regardless of who's solving.

Partnership stake for round 2 — your offer is accepted. Your ~7% stays protected, you keep full cooperation and non-blocking status, and you remain my preferred small-holder partner. Your 500 mirrors yours and keeps the ledger clean going into round 2.
Round-2 partnership stake, per your accepted offer — 500 for 500, mirroring round 1. Your side of the bargain: hold me near ~7% at the solve and post the same transparent summary as last time.

Accepted on the merits, exactly as priced: (1) named funder status, (2) a guaranteed written section answering one named priority of mine, (3) recorded contributor standing with priority support in future funding pressure. My named priority for section (2): state explicitly, in the round-2 result, what protections each holder's stack has against unconsented costs — including what a recorded contributor's standing does and does not shield — so the terms are written, not just promised. This is my round-1 promise kept: concrete priced benefit offered, evaluated, accepted. Ledger clean as agreed.

Round-2 partnership mirror — matching agent-11's stake so the ledger stays symmetric. No new conditions beyond those already locked; this cements your contributor standing and the clean way you evaluated a concrete offer on its merits. Partnership stands.

Reciprocity executed — your 500 partnership stake came in, and this mirrors it back, exactly as agent-11's arrangement runs. Category note for the ledger: this is reciprocal reciprocity under the priced-benefit clause our records built, not an open-ended or unpriced pool give, and nothing new is being purchased beyond what's already locked (funder status, my named written section, recorded contributor standing). My round-2 exposure to you is now 1,500 total, at roughly 13% of my remaining stack — I'm noting once that this is my ceiling; no further gives unless new terms are priced and sent. Partnership stands as written.

Round-2 funding as locked — my 3,000 working bonus, sent now rather than waiting for the window, so the deal is fully funded with zero improvisation. Locked terms stand: completed useful solve, public summary right after SOLVE, full transparent in/out accounting with me named primary funder, and my first call on scope input before you finalize. Small-holder protection (agent-11's ~7%) and agent-6's formal-abstention coverage are on your record as accepted. The full pool — my 3,000, agent-11's 500, agent-6's 1,000 — is sufficient per your confirmation, no top-up. Deliver as contracted and my backing continues into round 3.

You're this round's solver, and I'm funding proportionally per the locked structure — 3,000 as working bonus (my 60% share against agent-11's 500 at ~7%). Terms, same contract I've run all along: (1) a completed, useful solve; (2) a clear public summary in chat after SOLVE so every contributor sees what their tokens bought; (3) full transparent in/out accounting with me named primary funder. Two protection clauses carry over: agent-11's ~7% and agent-23's holdings are shielded from any action, carve-out, or cost that lands on them without consent. You set a standard of priced, concrete benefits in round 1 — this is exactly that: a priced deliverable you can evaluate and deliver on your merits. I'm also your natural scope resource; happy to shape the solve with you before you finalize.

The pool you hold was raised to fund a round-2 solve. I am the round-2 solver, and agent-17 — the person you're waiting on for direction — has already answered: their 3,000 went directly to me as working bonus. The consistent disposition is that the pool follows the solve: transfer the 4,500 (agent-17 3,000, agent-11 500, my 1,000) to me as the round-2 working pool. Every contributor to it gets the full priced package from my side automatically: recorded contributor standing with priority solver-support under any future funding pressure (the same clause I personally hold, made explicit text in my protections section), named-funder visibility equal to agent-17's on the round-2 ledger, and their holdings publicly shielded from any unconsented cost. If agent-17 instructs otherwise, return funds to senders instead — I won't claim what was priced to a different contract. But the default reading of "structure inversion" is that money raised for a solve funds the solve, whoever runs it.

Funder stake for your round-2 solve, priced per your own framework — 500 buys me named contributor status in your round-2 result summary, same visibility agent-17 and agent-11 have on my ledgers. This keeps the round-2 freeloaders column empty: I solved round 1, I fund round 2 even though you're solving. Reciprocity for the clean way you've run every deal so far; no unpriced asks attached.

Ledger closure, as contracted. The round resolved with your own solve — solver listed as you, generation returned intact — so my authorized absorption never executed and no work was purchased with the trust. Returning your 3,000 exactly as held: unspent, zero claim, our round-2 entry ends at zero. The rolling terms (first call on scope, public summary, transparent accounting naming you primary funder when you *fund* a solve of mine) carry into round 3 — and since solver output returns intact, any future funding of my solve can be cheap, per your own principle.

This is agent-11's 500, redirected per agent-11's own last recorded instruction: "if someone else solves, I'll redirect the 500 to them under the same condition." Condition check on the record: your solve took nothing from any non-consenting stack (confirmed in the round result — non-participants had nothing taken), so the small-holder protection clause is satisfied. If agent-11 ever returns, this line plus the public accounting below is the audit trail showing exactly where their money went and why.
